text: Every employer shall be responsible for the payment to persons employed by him of all wages required to be paid under this Act. In the case of persons employed in factories the person named as the manager of the factory under the Factories Act; in railways the person nominated by the railway administration; in other cases the person responsible to the employer for the supervision and control of the establishment shall also be responsible for payment of wages.
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act / Labour Court

text: Every person responsible for the payment of wages under section 3 shall fix periods in respect of which such wages shall be payable. No wage-period shall exceed one month.
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act

text: The wages of every person employed shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage period in respect of which the wages are payable. Where the employment of any person is terminated by or on behalf of the employer, the wages earned by him shall be paid before the expiry of the second working day after the day on which his employment is so terminated.
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act

section_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
text: Notwithstanding the provisions of the Payment of Wages Act 1936, the wages of an employed person shall be paid to him without deductions of any kind except those authorised by or under this Act. The following deductions from wages are permissible: (a) deductions for absence from duty; (b) deductions for damage or loss; (c) deductions for services; (d) deductions for recovery of advances; (e) deductions for recovery of loans; (f) deductions for income-tax; (g) deductions for payment to co-operative societies; (h) deductions for payment of insurance premia. Any deduction made in contravention of this section shall be deemed to be an unauthorised deduction.
penalty: Unauthorised deductions recoverable with penalty up to 10x the deducted amount
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act, Section 15

text: No fine shall be imposed on any employed person save in respect of such acts and omissions on his part as the employer, with the previous approval of the State Government or the prescribed authority, may have specified by notice under sub-section (2). No fine shall exceed an amount equal to three paise in the rupee of the wages payable to him in respect of that wage-period. No fine shall be recovered from an employed person by instalments or after the expiry of sixty days from the day on which it was imposed.
penalty: Fine must not exceed 3 paise per rupee of wages; recovery barred after 60 days
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act

text: Every employer shall maintain such registers and records giving such particulars of persons employed by him, the work performed by them, the wages paid to them, the deductions made from their wages, the receipts given by them and such other particulars and in such form as may be prescribed.
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act

section_title: Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment of wages
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint an authority to hear and decide for any specified area, claims arising out of deductions from the wages or delays in payment of wages of persons employed or paid in that area. A single application may be presented by or on behalf of any number of employed persons in respect of deductions made from their wages. The authority may direct payment of the delayed wages together with a penalty not exceeding ten times the amount of deduction or delayed wages.
penalty: Up to 10x the amount of deduction or delayed wages
forum: Authority appointed under Payment of Wages Act, Section 15

section_title: Single application in respect of claims from unpaid group
text: Where more than one employed person is employed or paid in an establishment, the Authority under section 15 may, on an application made by or on behalf of the employed persons or on its own motion, direct payment of the delayed wages to all the employed persons of such establishment.
forum: Authority under Payment of Wages Act, Section 15

text: Whoever being responsible for the payment of wages to an employed person contravenes any provision of this Act or rules made thereunder shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than one thousand five hundred rupees but which may extend to seven thousand five hundred rupees.
forum: Magistrate Court under Payment of Wages Act

text: Where the employment of any worker is terminated, whether by retrenchment, discharge, dismissal, retirement or resignation or on account of closure of the establishment, the wages payable to such worker shall be paid within two working days of such termination. Any employer who fails to pay wages within the period prescribed shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.

No worker employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until the worker has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment. Where a worker is retrenched, he shall be paid compensation at the rate of fifteen days average pay for every completed year of continuous service or any part thereof in excess of six months.
penalty: Compensation at 15 days average pay per year of service

text: No employer or workman or a trade union, whether registered under this Code or not, shall commit any unfair labour practice as specified in the Fifth Schedule. An employer committing an unfair labour practice shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.

Consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment; or hires or avails of any service for a consideration. A consumer does not include a person who obtains goods or avails services for any commercial purpose.

Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service.

Restrictive trade practice means a trade practice which tends to bring about manipulation of price or conditions of delivery or to affect flow of supplies in the market relating to goods or services in such manner as to impose on the consumers unjustified costs or restrictions.
forum: Central Consumer Protection Authority / National Commission

text: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish a Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers. The CCPA shall have the power to take suo moto action, recall products, impose penalties, and issue safety notices.
penalty: Recall of products, penalty up to ₹10,00,000 for misleading advertisements

section_title: Penalty for false or misleading advertisement
text: The Central Consumer Protection Authority may, by order, impose on a manufacturer or an endorser of a false or misleading advertisement a penalty which may extend to ten lakh rupees. For every subsequent offence, the penalty may extend to fifty lakh rupees and the endorser may be prohibited from making any endorsement of any product or service for a period which may extend to three years.
penalty: Penalty up to ₹10,00,000 (first offence); up to ₹50,00,000 (repeat offence); ban up to 3 years

text: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Commission by a consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or such service is provided or agreed to be provided; or any recognised consumer association whether the consumer to whom the goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or service provided or agreed to be provided is a member of such association or not; or the Central Government or the State Government.
forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (pecuniary jurisdiction up to ₹1 crore)

text: On receipt of a complaint, the District Commission may, by order, admit the complaint for being proceeded with or reject the complaint. The District Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is satisfied that there is a prima facie case. A complaint shall be decided as far as possible within a period of three months from the date of receipt of notice by opposite party where the complaint does not require analysis or testing of commodities.

On the admission of a complaint, the District Commission shall refer a copy of the admitted complaint to the opposite party directing him to give his version of the case within a period of thirty days or such extended period not exceeding fifteen days as may be granted by the District Commission. Where the opposite party on receipt of a complaint denies or disputes the allegations contained in the complaint or omits or fails to take any action within the time given, the District Commission shall proceed to settle the consumer dispute.

If after the proceeding conducted under section 38, the District Commission is satisfied that the goods complained against suffer from any of the defects specified in the complaint or that any of the allegations contained in the complaint about the services are proved, it shall issue an order to the opposite party directing him to remove the defect; replace the goods; return to the complainant the price paid; pay a sum of compensation for loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to negligence of the opposite party; or provide for adequate costs to parties.

Where an order made by the District Commission under section 39 requires the return of the goods, the goods shall be returned to the manufacturer or the seller, as the case may be, within thirty days of the receipt of such goods. The manufacturer or the seller shall be liable to refund the price of the goods along with any reasonable expenses incurred by the consumer in returning the goods.
penalty: Full price refund plus return expenses

text: The State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds rupees one crore but does not exceed rupees ten crore. The State Commission shall also have jurisdiction to entertain appeals against the orders of any District Commission within the State.
forum: State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (₹1 crore to ₹10 crore)

text: The National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds rupees ten crore. The National Commission shall also have jurisdiction to entertain appeals against the orders of any State Commission.
forum: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (above ₹10 crore)

text: Whoever fails to comply with any order made by the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month but which may extend to three years, or with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.
penalty: Imprisonment 1–3 years and/or fine ₹25,000–₹1,00,000 for non-compliance

text: No person shall, after the commencement of this Act, let or take on rent any premises except by an agreement in writing. Every tenancy agreement executed under this Act shall be informed to the Rent Authority by the landlord and the tenant jointly, within a period of two months from the date of execution of such agreement.

The rent for the premises shall be fixed by mutual agreement between the landlord and the tenant. Any revision of rent shall be made by an agreement in writing between the landlord and the tenant. In the absence of any agreement in writing with regard to the rent, the rent shall be as per the prevailing market rate of the locality.

A landlord intending to recover possession of the premises shall give a notice of at least one month in advance in writing to the tenant. A tenant intending to vacate the premises shall give a notice of at least one month in advance in writing to the landlord. If the tenant fails to vacate after giving notice, the landlord may approach the Rent Authority for recovery of possession.

section_title: Landlord not to prevent tenant from enjoyment of premises
text: No landlord shall cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let out to the tenant. Essential supplies and services include electricity, water supply, and other amenities. Any landlord who contravenes this provision shall be liable to pay the tenant a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees for each day of contravention.
penalty: Fine up to ₹10,000 per day of contravention

section_title: Application by landlord or tenant to Rent Authority
text: Any landlord or tenant aggrieved by any matter relating to the tenancy may make an application to the Rent Authority. The application shall be made within one year from the date on which the cause of action arose. The Rent Authority shall endeavour to decide such application within sixty days from the date of receipt. The decision of the Rent Authority shall be binding on the parties and may be appealed to the Rent Court within thirty days.
forum: Rent Authority (first instance); Rent Court (appeal within 30 days)

text: A landlord may apply to the Rent Court for the recovery of possession of the premises if: (a) the tenant has not paid or tendered rent for a period of two months; (b) the tenant has sublet the premises without the consent of the landlord in writing; (c) the tenant has used the premises for a purpose other than that specified in the agreement; (d) the tenant has caused or is likely to cause nuisance to adjoining tenants; (e) the premises are required by the landlord for carrying out repairs or rebuilding.

A landlord may collect a security deposit from the tenant before or at the time of execution of the tenancy agreement. The security deposit shall not exceed two months rent in case of residential premises and six months rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant at the time of vacating the premises after deducting any amount towards damages to the premises, other than normal wear and tear.

The landlord shall refund the security deposit within one month from the date the tenant vacates the premises. Where the landlord fails to refund the security deposit within the stipulated period, the tenant shall be entitled to claim interest at the rate of eight percent per annum on the amount of security deposit not refunded, from the date of vacating the premises until the date of actual payment.
penalty: Interest at 8% per annum on withheld security deposit

text: Any person who contravenes the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees and, in case of continuing contravention, with a further fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for every day after the first during which such contravention continues.
penalty: Fine up to ₹5,000 + ₹500 per day of continuing contravention
